evidence: Independent-reader numerical audit and propagation of sampled JPL direction/range residuals through a conditional atmosphere/source model.
time_scale: TT; no UTC or future leap-second assumption enters this comparison.
frame: MOON_ME, east-positive longitude; local topocentric geometry subtracts the lunar observer position.

conventions.direction_only: Both ephemerides use identical native Earth/Moon and Sun/Moon ranges; only the directions differ. This also covers rows without independent ranges.
conventions.directions_and_geometric_ranges: Only the 2,507 epochs with both independently sampled JPL geometric ranges; directions and ranges are changed together.
conventions.earth_source: Phase/bright-limb orientation are recomputed from each topocentric geometry. Normalized Lambert spatial weights multiply the exported measured spectral phase response exactly once.
conventions.dilution: Solar inverse square from Sun/observer; Earth solid-angle ratio to the reference distance, multiplied by Sun/Earth inverse square.
conventions.comparator: JPL observer coordinates are apparent and light-time corrected; native vectors are instantaneous. Residuals retain that convention difference.
conventions.interpolation: Linear in native source elevation and empirical phase nodes, matching evaluator.mjs. Disk quadrature orders 12 and 24.
conventions.eclipses: Potential Sun/Earth angular-disk overlaps are excluded from error summaries; eclipse attenuation is not solved.
conventions.error_reading: Observed maxima at saved samples only; RMS describes this deliberately nonuniform sample, not a climatological average. Small source-relative errors can shift grazing brightness thresholds greatly. This audit does not assign a uniform timing accuracy.
conventions.boundary: No observational validation of the atmosphere or future Earth cloud/surface pattern; spatial Earth spectrum is uniform. Terrain, refraction, polarization and finite-distance variation within the atmospheric shell remain outside this response.

disk_quadrature.evidence: Quadrature-order sensitivity for the same exported response tables; order 24 is a numerical comparator, not exact truth.

historical_solar_regression.evidence: Sampled regression between distinct numerical producers on their saved elevation nodes; no universal pass/fail tolerance.

normalization.sun_distance: 1 AU, inverse-square factor fixed to one

historical.disk_method: 12 strips across the visible solar disk for attenuation; the diffuse scattering phase uses the disk-center direction.
historical.convergence_rule: Surface increment test applies to elevations at least -24 degrees, together with a whole-field maximum test; retained tolerance 2e-5. One retained channel continued beyond the initial order cap to order 104.
historical.published_readout: Published diffuse flux integrates the directional atlas; the product separately retains moment-grid diffuse flux. Both are compared.
historical.sea_curve_readout: Moment diffuse flux linearly interpolated in elevation, plus a log-interpolated direct-normal beam times sin(elevation), set to zero at and below zero elevation. No stellar/airglow floor is included in this solar-only curve.

calendar.disk_method: Point-source transport convolved over a finite uniform disk after export; direct and diffuse source-elevation responses are both integrated.
calendar.convergence_rule: The point-source surface increment test spans the full -90 to +90 degree source-elevation grid, with the recorded tolerance and whole-field maximum test.

historical_solar_regression.interpretation: A difference includes source-disk treatment, retained scattering orders, readout and interpolation changes. Agreement would be numerical consistency, not independent physical validation. No reference is extrapolated beyond its saved elevation support.

golden_reading_rule: Feed geometry, includeEarth and order to lightAt. native_ephemeris cases also permit end-to-end geometry+light comparison at their TT Julian date and coordinates.
